title: Computational Cognitive Science (9.66J / 9.660 / 6.804J) — CBMM course entry page
authors: Joshua Tenenbaum (instructor named on the page)
institution: MIT Center for Brains, Minds and Machines (CBMM)
description: Catalogue-style entry page for the current MIT course: numbers 9.66J, 9.660, 6.804J; instructor Joshua Tenenbaum; semester listed as Fall 2021; prerequisites (9.40, 6.008, 6.036, 6.041B, 18.05 or permission; basic probability and statistics; programming); four problem sets and a final modeling project; a topic outline covering probabilistic generative models, structured symbolic systems, hierarchical models and approximate inference, with applications to perception, language, common-sense reasoning and theory of mind. The only course link is to an MIT Stellar site (institutional login).
rightsNotes: The page carries a CBMM copyright notice and a Terms of Use link; no open licence. Reference-only: cited as the owner's entry point and for the current course's scope, never imported.

The page does not provide lecture videos, slides, a syllabus file or OCW materials for this offering. Public teaching material for the course exists only as the Fall 2004 OCW publication (source mit-cocosci-2004).
